Menu names may differ a little: Google changes them often.
How much of the reply to collect before it starts playing. More means smoother sound on a weak connection, but the reply starts a little later.
“Listening” and “On it” spoken aloud, or two short tones instead of words (the same for every language). Glow only — only the light indication on the panel, and commands run silently.

Where a spoken “navigate to …” goes when you do not name the app. Say “in Google Maps”, “in Waze”, “in HERE WeGo” or “in Organic Maps” and the assistant uses that one this time; without it — the navigator chosen here. HERE WeGo and Organic Maps only open the search for the address: pick the result and tap Route.

The session stops by itself — like STOP — after this long without the car browser (or any other viewer) connected. For when you leave the car and forget to press STOP: otherwise the encoder, VPN and hotspot keep running in the background. Off keeps the old behaviour: the session lives until you press STOP.
The session will come up by itself as soon as you open the app — no need to press START.

TeslaDroid GPS Shield safeguards navigation apps (such as Waze and Google Maps) from satellite signal anomalies, jamming, and spoofing attacks. When disruption or spoofed trajectory jumps are detected, the system immediately switches to fused cellular network and Wi-Fi positioning. Once clean satellite reception is verified, navigation smoothly returns to standard GPS.

Puts the Android status bar (and the nav bar, where the firmware provides one) on the car display. Waze and other apps no longer need it for their margins: since 4.962 they get the same margins without the bars, so the search panel, buttons and speedometer stay in place anyway. Turn it on only if you want to see the Android status bar in the car. Takes effect at the next START. On Pixel with Android 17 the bars also bring the launcher’s taskbar at the bottom. On Samsung with gesture navigation the back gesture on the phone itself may die after a lock — stop the stream, then lock and unlock.
Darkens the phone screen without stopping the stream. Any touch on the screen brings the brightness back.

Works together with “System bars on the car display”. Some phones (Pixel on Android 17) add a bottom bar — the launcher’s taskbar — next to the status bar, and it cannot be switched off separately. With this switch the car display is made taller by its height and the car screen simply does not show that strip; the status bar stays. The bar’s buttons will not be available in the car. Takes effect from the next START.
A small block of figures in the corner of the picture: frames per second, bitrate, delay. Useful when the picture stutters; most drivers keep it off.

The Samsung keyboard arrives on the car display with an old layout — cropped and unresponsive. The reset costs one cold start of the keyboard at the beginning of a session, while it is not yet visible.
The list of installed apps: tick the ones whose tiles should be in the menu on the car screen. The rest are simply hidden there — they stay on the phone.
A small window over the picture: kilometres, time in motion and average speed for the trip. Tap it to switch between trips A and B, hold to reset the current one.

Some apps ask for portrait orientation, and on some phones the picture ends up sideways along with the touches. With this checkbox the system refuses them the rotation, and they are shown straight, with margins at the edges.

Brings everything up at once: the address for the car, the car display and sound. Then open the address shown at the top in the Tesla browser.\nUsually there is nothing to wait for: after a reboot the app prepares everything by itself, as soon as the phone sees Wi-Fi. If START says the rights are missing, the phone has forgotten the app — open the readiness list and pair again, at home, on Wi-Fi.
Ends the session and closes the apps that were running on the car display. The phone returns to its usual state.

The strip with the clock, phone status, favourites and buttons stands by the left edge of the car screen rather than the right — closer to the driver. Swipe it towards its edge to collapse it, the tab brings it back. The app-menu button: tap — the app grid, hold — running apps.

Checks whether a newer version is out; if so, an update button appears. Update only on Wi-Fi: after an update TeslaDroid is started again via Wireless debugging. The session is best stopped beforehand.
Marks the app as the one that starts automatically after START.

Touches, gestures and the Android keyboard all work on the car screen — exactly as on the phone itself.\nIf on Xiaomi the picture is there but touches do not go through, turn on “USB debugging (Security settings)” in developer options: without it MIUI does not let touches through. TeslaDroid will point to it both on the phone and in the car.
Hold it to pick any other installed app for auto start.
They start the app straight on the car screen, not on the phone.
Press this button before you reproduce the problem. The app will start recording in detail.
Do in the car whatever does not work: start the app that ends up sideways, wait until the picture falls apart, and so on. A few minutes is plenty.
The same button, now it reads “Stop collecting”. After it, two files are ready on the phone.
The usual “Share” will open — select your preferred email or messaging app and send it to Support: dev@tesla-droid.app. It is a small file, it always gets through.
The same, but as a separate message: the file weighs several megabytes. Send it second, after the log.
Once both files are sent, press “Clear previous diagnostics” — they take up space on the phone. The button is grey when there is nothing left to clear.
Just send the log — it already holds everything the app recorded since its last start.
If the problem cannot be reproduced

✦ to start, ✦ again to end. Speak as to a person; it finds the end of a phrase itself and picks up your language. To interrupt, tap the panel.\n10 seconds of silence and the conversation closes by itself (6 s if music was paused for it). Not a bug: this way no quota or money is spent on minutes when you are silent. Next question — ✦ again, connecting takes about a second. If replies break up on a weak connection, raise “Reply delay”.

“No key” — enter the Gemini key here.
No ✦ button in the browser — turn it on here; it appears within seconds without reloading the page.
The car browser refused the microphone — on Intel that is normal, choose the “phone” or “auto” microphone; on Ryzen clear the Tesla browser data (Controls → Service → Clear Browser Data) and allow again.
The conversation closed after silence — as intended (10 s).
The wake word triggers on similar phrases — raise “Wake word threshold”; it does not hear you — lower it.
Replies break up or arrive late — weak connection; raise “Reply delay”.
“Model not found” — press “Check key”, it picks a current model.
An error about limits (429) — the free tier’s daily quota is used up; it comes back the next day, or switch to the paid 3.8.

Tap the ✦ star in the control strip on the car screen. The microphone picks up your voice and sends it to Google; the answer comes back as sound and plays in the speakers right away. Music pauses for the conversation and resumes after it (unless the assistant started something else itself). At the bottom of the screen is a panel: a status word (listening / hearing you / thinking / speaking) and an equalizer. The key stays on the phone; with the car microphone it goes only to your own page in the car browser. The conversation is between you and Google; our server takes no part in it.

Tesla with the AMD Ryzen computer and software 2026.26 or newer — the car’s own microphone can be used; the browser asks for permission each time, tap “Allow”. The price: it mutes the car’s media for the conversation.
Tesla on Intel — the browser has no microphone (Tesla’s decision). Then you speak into the phone in its holder, and the answer still comes from the car speakers. If the phone is far away, raise “Phone sensitivity” (×2 by default, up to ×16).
In both cases you interrupt the assistant by tapping the panel, not by voice — otherwise it would hear itself from the speakers.
The “Source” choice: auto (the car first, the phone if refused), Tesla, phone. The wake word always listens through the phone microphone.

The “Model” button shows the live list of Google Live API models for your key. Two matter:
• gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio — the Google AI Studio free tier: no card, daily limits; enough for everyday questions on the road, and when the limit is reached the conversation ends with an error and comes back the next day.
• gemini-3.8-live — works and talks noticeably better, but it is paid: you need to put a little money on your own key (Google AI Studio → Billing). Roughly $0.005 per minute of your voice and $0.018 per minute of reply; an active month is a few dollars.
Either way the bill is yours — we add nothing and receive nothing.
Everything you say after ✦ goes to Google — their service, their rules. The key is stored locally on the phone only; TeslaDroid does not collect or transmit conversation data.

Hold ✦ for about 3 seconds — the frame turns amber, and from then on the words “hey tesla” open a conversation, no tap needed. It listens through the phone microphone; the wake-word model is our own and runs on the phone, no audio goes online. Hold again to turn it off; the mode is remembered between trips.\n“Wake word threshold” is the sensitivity: lower triggers more easily but also on similar phrases; higher needs clearer speech. “Waiting for a command” — how long to wait after the word if you stay silent before closing the conversation.

A voice assistant right in the Tesla browser — Google Gemini. You talk, it answers by voice through the car speakers, no phone in hand. Questions on the road, translation, explanations, web search (Google Search built in) — short and conversational: it knows you are driving, the current date and time, what is playing and which navigator you prefer.\nActions on the phone: “navigate to …” — Waze or Google Maps on the car screen; “call …” — a contact from your address book via the car’s Bluetooth; “play …” — a song or artist in YouTube Music; “open YouTube …” — a search on the car screen; “open …” — any installed app on the car screen; “close …” — remove it from the car screen. Nothing else — no messages, no control of the car itself.
For Gemini to play music, make calls and build routes, set it up: the “%1$s” button under the switch.

✦ or “hey tesla” starts a conversation; ✦ or “hey tesla” again ends it. Music pauses during the conversation and resumes afterwards. During the conversation the phone\'s volume buttons change Gemini\'s volume, and it is remembered for next time.
✦ or “hey tesla” opens Google\'s Gemini Live right on the car screen — a voice conversation, no API key.
PCM is not compressed at all and costs no CPU. Opus compresses tenfold, but the codec is software and heats the phone even when the picture is still. Opus is worth it only on weak Wi-Fi.

Sound in the car browser is received by a separate thread instead of the main one, which also draws the picture. When the Tesla browser freezes for a moment while drawing, the sound no longer breaks because of it.\nNew and off by default: turn it on if the music stutters or “quacks”. If it does not start in the car, the page silently returns to the usual way.
Sharpness of the moving picture. Lower means visible blocks in complex scenes, but the phone runs cooler.

How long to hold the video back so that it matches the sound. The hold works only while sound is playing and you are not touching the screen: the moment you tap, the picture catches up at once, so taps respond without delay. Two seconds after the last touch, the video smoothly falls back in sync with the sound. Maps and menus without sound are never held.
How long until the phone screen goes dark during a session. The stream keeps going, a touch brings the brightness back.
Smoothness of motion. Higher is smoother, but heavier on Wi-Fi and the battery.

The band of the phone hotspot the car connects to. 5 GHz has less interference, so sound and picture flow more evenly. “As on the phone” leaves the hotspot settings untouched — choose it if the car does not see the network on 5 GHz.
When another app opens on the car screen, music may pause. Tick the apps that should let it keep playing when you switch to them — a navigation app, for example.
The size of the app tiles in the menu on the car screen. Bigger ones are easier to hit while driving; smaller ones fit more apps on one screen.
The size of everything on the car screen. A smaller number means bigger elements and less fits.

2. Settings → Developer options → Wireless debugging — turn it on

Android has no shortcut here — developer options will open, and there you have to find “Wireless debugging” and turn it on.\n\nAdding that tile to the quick settings is faster: next time it is one move, with no wandering through settings.
This is how TeslaDroid gets shell rights. It switches itself off after a reboot — TeslaDroid switches it back on by itself once paired.
The button opens the app card — there: Battery → “Allow background activity”, set it to “Unrestricted”.
Without it the system removes the app during the drive, and the stream dies.
Settings → About phone → tap the build number seven times.
Without them there is no wireless debugging, and without that TeslaDroid cannot get shell rights.
They keep the streaming service alive. Without them Android will stop it.

One time only. Open Developer options → Wireless debugging → “Pair device with pairing code”, and type the six digits here. The phone must be on some Wi-Fi network — any one; while it is sharing its own, this does not work.
Without them there is no separate display for the car — only a mirror of the phone screen, portrait, with black bars.
Shizuku asks separately for every app.
Open Shizuku and press “Start via wireless debugging”.
It has to be started after every phone reboot — that is an Android limitation, and without root there is no way around it.
You already have it, so it stays as a fallback. TeslaDroid no longer needs it: rights now come from the phone’s own ADB.
TeslaDroid couldn’t turn it on by itself. In developer options, turn on “USB debugging” — no cable is needed.
Keeps TeslaDroid’s service alive when the phone switches from Wi-Fi to its hotspot in the car. Without it the service dies together with wireless debugging.

In developer options, turn on “USB debugging (Security settings)” — just below “USB debugging”. MIUI may ask you to sign in to your Mi account and insert a SIM card.

"During the session the phone plays no notification sounds — banners stay, both on the phone and in the car.
